# Internet Archive

> > Internet Archive is a non-profit digital library providing universal access to preserved websites, books, audio, video, and government publications through the Wayback Machine and other archival services.

Founded by Brewster Kahle, Internet Archive serves as a federal depository library and operates the Wayback Machine, the world's largest web archive. The organization focuses on digital preservation, providing free access to humanity's cultural and informational heritage.

## Core Services & Search

- [Wayback Machine Search](http://search.archive.org/): Main search interface for accessing Wayback Machine digital archive collections and historical web snapshots
- [Wayback Machine Advanced Search](https://archive.org/web/web-advancedsearch.php): Advanced search interface for precise Wayback Machine web archive retrieval with filtering options
- [How To Search the Internet Archive](https://help.archive.org/help/how-to-search-the-internet-archive/): Guide to searching Internet Archive collections using metadata, text search, and discovery tools

## Getting Started & Support

- [Wayback Machine General Information](https://help.archive.org/help/wayback-machine-general-information/): FAQ and comprehensive overview of Wayback Machine functionality, features, and digital preservation methods
- [Uploading – A Basic Guide](https://help.archive.org/help/uploading-a-basic-guide/): Tutorial for uploading files, managing metadata, and contributing content to Internet Archive

## News & Milestones

- [Internet Archive 25th Anniversary](https://anniversary.archive.org/): Celebration of Internet Archive's 25th anniversary and institutional achievements in digital preservation and universal access
- [Internet Archive Designated as Federal Depository Library](https://blog.archive.org/2025/07/24/internet-archive-designated-as-a-federal-depository-library/): News announcement: Internet Archive officially designated as a federal depository library for government publications
